text:
Anna: heads-up — during Mistral-v2 onboarding I hit a weird token-id collision causing repeated pad/sentinel output in generation. samples show '<pad>' appearing in the middle of sentences. anyone seen pad <-> sentinel aliasing before? :thinking:
Sam: can you paste the tokenizer slice around special tokens? quick dump is fine.
Anna: pasted small extract: ```{'<pad>': 0, '<s>': 1, '</s>': 2, '<sentinel_1>': 50256, '<sentinel_2>': 50257}```
Kai: for Qwen we remapped some special ids to the high range during conversion; possible overlap if one model uses 0 for pad and the other puts pad into the sentinel range.
Diego: saw similar in a quant run — generation had repeated sentinel tokens and kv-cache shape warnings. attached log snippet: ```WARNING: AttnCache mismatch: key shape (12, 64) vs expected (12, 63)```
Anna: repro script I ran: ```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
tok = Tokenizer.from_file('mistral-v2.json')
print(tok.encode('hello world').ids)
``` result: `[101, 102, 0, 110, ...]` where 0 is pad injected mid-stream.
eval-bot: regression alert: eval/qa-200 -- rouge_l delta -3.4%, perplexity +1.8 vs baseline after quant + tokenizer merge.
Sam: theory: our conversion step for qwen set pad id into a high value (50256) but later quant pipeline truncates/mangles ids into uint8 during some serialization step, causing collisions (id % 256). That would alias pad<->sentinel after quant.
Kai: that matches the cache shape warning — if token ids shift, KV indexing mismatches. Also note some tokenizers use negative pad internally; mixing signed/unsigned storage is dangerous.
Anna: quick audit command I ran: `python tools/token_id_audit.py --models mistral-v2 qwen-1.2 --check-sentinel` output: ```mistral-v2: pad=0 sentinels=[50256..50270]
qwen-1.2: pad=50256 sentinels=[50257..50270]
collision: pad==sentinel[0] -> True```
Diego: ouch. immediate mitigation options?
Sam: mitigation plan: (1) enforce canonical pad=0 during conversion for all onboarded models unless explicit customer requirement, (2) add a tokenizer metadata validation gate in CI, (3) add a defensive layer in runtime to treat pad token id specially in KV-cache (e.g., treat as -1 / masked).
Kai: + add a unit test in quant pipeline: roundtrip ids -> bytes -> ids for max id ranges and ensure no wraparound. Also add an assert during gguf/pt conversion that no special id collides with pad.
Anna: I pushed a conversion patch that remaps qwen pad->0 and shifts sentinel range by +10 to avoid overlap; PR #2128 includes a test and tokenizer audit tool changes. Holding Mistral and Qwen dedicated rollouts until we merge. cc @eng-releases.
Diego: quick patch on runtime treating pad as masked fixed streaming alignment for a few failing jobs. but it's a band-aid.
Sam: can someone run the full eval after #2128 lands? want to confirm rouge/perp back to baseline.
Anna: will queue full eval on nightly and post results. For now added checklist item: "token id audit: special tokens vs pad" to onboarding doc.
Kai: nice. once merged, also add a small fuzz test that encodes >1000 random strings and checks kv-cache index stability across quantized vs fp32 runs.
Diego: thumbs-up. if any production signals degrade, fallback to hosted small model until fixed. :thumbsup:
Anna: thanks — I'll update thread when eval completes.
